title: DPP publisher key policy, version 1
description: The bounded set of keys authorised to countersign admitted states and anchors for an operator or a federation (spec/services.md section 1). Each policy version is a complete statement; a new version names the digest of the one it supersedes and is authorised by a signature that the previous version's rules accept. A retired key keeps authenticating the states it signed while active, and a state is checked against the key active at the state's time, never against the newest list. Canonical JSON for this document: object keys sorted recursively by code point, no whitespace, arrays in order, undefined members omitted, and only strings, booleans and safe integers as values.

items.description: Operator identifiers: a DID or a named deployment. Operator identity is distinct from every publisher key below.

topics.description: The topics the policy covers; absent means every topic the operators serve.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the superseded policy's canonical JSON, signatures included, so history is a chain and no version is silently rewritten.

key.description: Compressed public key. For tm_dpp this is the identity key the service's BRC-42 countersignature derives from; for anchors it is the service identity the anchor's field-8 key derives from.

operator.description: Which operator holds the key; absent in a single-operator scope.

retiredAt.description: After this instant the key authorises nothing new; states it signed while active remain authentic.

custody.description: Where the key lives, in the vocabulary of spec/custody.md section 5; informative.

kind.description: genesis: the first version of a scope, authorised by the identity key of an operator named in scope.operators; rotation: the same operators replace keys, authorised by a key active under the superseded version and, in a federation, countersigned by another operator's identity key; handover: the operator set changes, authorised by a key active under the superseded version and countersigned by an incoming operator's identity key.

suite.description: ECDSA over SHA-256 of the canonical JSON of this document without authorisation.value and authorisation.countersignature, DER encoded; the countersignature, when present, is over the same bytes.
